All 42 assessors: seven octahedra

The 42 assessors, one octahedron per strut, at seven corners of a cube; the eighth corner is e₀. A picture shows a structure; it is not evidence that the structure means anything beyond its definition.

← Box-kite gallery

orbit: off
About this visual

What you are looking at. All 42 assessors at once: seven octahedra, one per strut s = 1…7, set at seven corners of a cube. The cube corner is the binary expansion of s (x = bit 1, y = bit 2, z = bit 4); the eighth corner, s = 0, is left empty and marked e0, the place the geometry does not occupy.

How to read it. Choose a strut to isolate it or leave 'all'. Drag to turn, wheel to zoom, double-click to reset. Click a vertex for its assessor, its strut and its four neighbours. The numbers under the picture are computed from the engine's glued graph: 42 vertices, 84 edges, and the count of edges that cross between kites.

What it shows. That the 42 assessors are the disjoint union of seven octahedra: every one of the 84 edges is inside a strut, none crosses between two (cross-strut edges = 0). So the Laplacian spectrum is the octahedral spectrum seven times over: 7 zero modes, 21 at 4, 14 at 6.

What it does not show. How the seven kites are glued into one geometry. The engine does not do it yet (its own stated open item), and the picture does not either: the cube positions are a drawing choice made from the bits of s, not part of the engine's graph. No line between kites is drawn because the engine has none.

Numbers to check. 42 vertices, 84 edges, 0 cross-strut edges, 7 components; zero modes 7 (one per kite), eigenvalue 4 with multiplicity 21 and 6 with multiplicity 14.

running self-check…

Code and data. Everything shown is recomputed in the browser by bk.js (the Cayley–Dickson table by doubling, every product, the group by enumeration) and compared with the numbers the Python engine baked into bk_data.js.

  • ValaQuenta/modules/box_kite/maths.py: the Python engine these pages port and check against (Cayley–Dickson table, assessors, box-kites, associator, the labelled group)
  • ValaQuenta/wiki/box_kite.md: the engine's record page, including 'The group, enumerated'
  • Ainulindale/wiki/84_the_box_kite_debugger.md: the narrative of the box-kite as a debugger
  • ValaQuenta/tests/test_box_kite.py: the tests, including an independent recursive Cayley–Dickson product
